title: Judge athena.toml by the candidate's schema without host builds
summary: The landing gate (content.rs) parses a changed athena.toml/defaults.toml with the running schema, so a commit that adds a section together with its schema is refused; admission fixed this by building the candidate's athena-data on the host. Fix both at the root: add a test in the candidate's own athena-data that parses the repo's athena.toml and defaults.toml, which runs only in the agent sandbox. When the commit changes crates/athena-data/, gate and admission rely on that sandboxed test and never compile candidate code. Otherwise they parse with the running schema. Audience: Athena operators and the verifier of parallel jobs.

defaults_applied.how: Regression tests for gate and admission plus an athena-data config test; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Fix the gate and admission with one shared rule instead of patching the gate alone.
Criteria check that schema-plus-config commits pass and bad configs still fail, by running tests.
Design note and CHANGELOG written for outside readers.
The rule is enforced by a test in the repo, not prose.
One focused change on the two checks and their shared helper.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The agent sandbox runs cargo test on the candidate, so a repo test is the way to judge the candidate's schema without host compilation.
Reading at base: gate content.rs lines 84-104 use Config::parse and DefaultsModel::parse (running schema); admission.rs check_with_candidate_schema builds candidate code with cargo run on the host.
The host-side builder (check_with_candidate_schema, CHECK_MAIN) is removed, not kept as a fallback.
When crates/athena-data/ is unchanged, the running schema equals the parent's, so host parsing is safe and still catches bad files.
A schema-changing commit whose sandboxed test does not run or fails is caught by the existing check/test gate; the decision is recorded in docs/design and CHANGELOG.
Governance files athena.toml, defaults.toml and workflows need no change.

acceptance_criteria.text: Gate regression test: a commit that adds an athena.toml section and the matching athena-data schema change in one commit produces no Configuration violation from athena-gate content::check, while the same athena.toml change without a schema change is still refused with the parse error. Run: cargo test -p athena-gate.

Admission test: a candidate changing both crates/athena-data/ and athena.toml is admitted without any process being spawned to build candidate code, and an unknown section with no schema change is still a violation. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
admission.rs no longer contains check_with_candidate_schema, CHECK_MAIN, or any Command::new(cargo) use on candidate files; grep shows none in athena-core or athena-gate.

A test in crates/athena-data parses the repository's athena.toml and defaults.toml with that crate's own schema and fails if either does not parse, so a candidate's sandboxed cargo test judges its own schema. Run: cargo test -p athena-data.
Both checks use one shared rule for deciding when to defer to the sandboxed test, so gate and admission cannot diverge. Run: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt --check all pass.
A short design note records the decision with alternatives (host build, sandbox build, lenient parse) and states why candidate code is never built on the host; CHANGELOG notes the change.

out_of_scope: Parallel drain behavior, panic isolation, and the '(could run in parallel)' label from job xh54.
Re-running job qcrz or landing the [parallel] section.
Sandboxing or changing the agent sandbox.
departures: Slightly higher cost than reference: two crates, a design decision, and new tests across gate and admission.
